title: Streaming auth orchestration and ergonomic downgrade to async-generator parity
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Consumers reported subtle incompatibilities between the TypeScript streaming API and the Python/Go SDKs when token refresh or credential handoff happened mid-stream. The root cause is duplicated token-refresh logic in streaming connectors and an ergonomic surface that exposes a low-level push/callback model that is hard to handle in some runtimes. This PR centralizes orchestration for streaming auth, introduces a light ergonomic downgrade path (async-generator wrapper) for older runtimes and establishes a cross-SDK compatibility contract. Scope: 1) Add a small 'AuthOrchestrator' in the TS SDK that owns token refresh logic for streaming connectors and exposes a consumer-friendly hook for credential handoff. 2) Provide an optional async-generator wrapper (streamToAsyncGenerator) that downgrades push-style streams to async generators for parity with Python's async iterator and Go's channel-based helpers. 3) Coordinate version bump and compatibility notes for Python/Go SDK teams (see linked linear tasks). 4) Add tests and update examples. Checklist: - [x] Implement AuthOrchestrator with pluggable token provider adapter - [x] Implement async-generator downgrade helper + docs - [x] Add unit + integration tests covering mid-stream token rotation and reattach semantics - [x] Update changelog and bump package version to 1.14.0 - [x] Coordinate companion PRs in python & go (ENG-1124, ENG-1188) Compatibility considerations: the orchestrator is opt-in; existing consumers keep current behavior unless they enable orchestration via the client config option 'streamAuth: { orchestrate: true }'. Default remains conservative (no behavioral change). When enabled, the orchestrator will: - serialize token refresh so only a single token refresh occurs concurrently for multi-connection use cases - expose an idempotent 'attachCredentials' hook called by the runtime before resume attempts - fallback to the async-generator wrapper if the consumer passed a legacy callback consumer or if runtime is Node 12 (older environments). Cross-SDK coordination: we worked with the Go and Python SDK owners to land companion adapters: python PR #533218 adds the generator-first helper; go PR #150412 exposes a channel shim; this TS change intentionally mirrors API ergonomics rather than copy implementation details to keep each SDK idiomatic. Risks & mitigations: - potential regressions in high-throughput streaming workloads: mitigated by a micro-benchmark and opt-in flag - complexity for custom credential providers: addressed by a documented adapter interface and two shipped adapters (default KMS adapter + in-memory token cache) - flakiness in CI: added test harness that can simulate mid-stream credential swap and network hiccups Notes for reviewers: please pay attention to the attachCredentials semantics in AuthOrchestrator.attachForResume; the idempotency guarantees are essential for safe retries. Also verify the async-generator wrapper properly passes back errors and final metadata in the same shape as the native push stream. Release notes: bump TS SDK to v1.14.0; add 'streamAuth.orchestrate' opt-in flag and 'streamToAsyncGenerator' helper; backwards compatible by default.
